artworks.title: Odysseus Returns Chryseis to Her Father
artworks.description: Claude stages the Iliad's first reconciliation as a luminous seaport: Odysseus escorts Chryseis back to Chryses amid classical quays and morning light. The priest's daughter whose ransom opened Book I becomes a quiet figure in a vast harbour world. Oil on canvas, Musée du Louvre, Paris.

artworks.title: Chryseis Returned to Her Father
artworks.description: West's grand-manner canvas reunites Chryses with his daughter after Apollo's plague forced Agamemnon's hand — the priest's prayer answered, the captive restored beneath the god's statue. A companion piece in the New-York Historical Society's collection, it treats Chryseis as the moral hinge of Iliad Book I.

artworks.title: Chryses Ransoming Chryseis from Agamemnon
artworks.description: Side A of an Apulian red-figure volute-krater from Taranto shows Chryses pleading before Agamemnon for his daughter's return — the Homeric embassy that Agamemnon refuses, unleashing Apollo's arrows. Chryseis stands as the contested prize at the origin of the Achaean quarrel. Musée du Louvre, Paris.

popCulture.title: Iliad
popCulture.creator: Homer
popCulture.description: Book 1 opens on Chryses' daughter: Agamemnon's refusal to return Chryseis brings Apollo's plague, and her ransom is the first quarrel that unmakes the Achaean camp.

popCulture.title: Chryseis
popCulture.description: The priest's daughter of Chryse remains the Iliad's opening wound — the captive whose release costs Agamemnon his honor and Achilles his prize.
